newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gold demand rose six pct in 1996 - WGC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gold demand rose six pct in 1996 - WGC.

text.p: Demand for gold in the United States reached a record 345.3 tonnes in 1996, six percent above the previous record set in 1995, World Gold Council (WGC) said Wednesday.

"Jewelry demand, up five percent to 320 tonnes during 1996, was once again the mainspring of the steady growth in US gold consumption," WGC economist for the Americas Richard Scott Ram said at a briefing on the publication of the WGC's fourth-quarter 1996 demand trends survey.
"The expansion in gold jewellery sales (in the US) is now in its fifth year and shows no signs of slackening," he said.
The value of gold jewelry sales to consumers for the year as a whole rose five percent over the already strong level of 1995, according to retail audit figures, WGC said.

Preliminary reports from the "non-store" retail survey, which covers television shopping channels and catalogues, indicate dollar sales were up six percent over 1995 after the first nine months of the year, with the total for the year projected at $1.1 billion.
Total gold jewelry sales amounted to $11.3 billion, up five percent on 1995.
"The U.S. jewelry market is a 320-tonne market annually, and is the largest in the world and has had 21 consecutive quarters of growth," WGC Americas region chief executive Michael Carlerin said.
Dental demand for gold in the U.S. rose seven percent in 1996 to 13.4 tonnes.
Investment demand for bullion coins rose to 11.9 tonnes compared to the 1995 level of 10.7 tonnes.
